title: Shortest shelf with every part
prompt:
shelf lists parts in order and kit lists the parts you need; return the shortest contiguous slice of shelf that contains every kit part with at least its multiplicity.

- shelf and kit each have 1 to 100,000 ASCII letters; matching is case-sensitive.
- If several shortest slices exist, return the leftmost one. Return "" if no slice covers kit.
hints: For each right end, the best left end is as far right as possible while the slice still covers the kit.
Expand right until the window covers kit, then shrink from the left while it still covers, recording the window each time.

Track need[c] (kit count minus window count) and missing = number of kit characters still uncovered. When missing hits 0, shrink while need[shelf[left]] < 0, record the window if strictly shorter, then drop shelf[left] and continue.

solution.explanation: need goes negative for surplus characters, so the left edge can drop them without breaking coverage; it stops at the first character the window truly needs. Each covering window is recorded at its tightest, then that needed character is released to search for the next one. Updating only on a strictly shorter length keeps the leftmost minimum because windows are found in increasing order of right end.

complexity.notes: Each index enters and leaves the window at most once. The map holds one entry per distinct character seen.

followUps: If shelf is huge and kit uses few distinct characters, how could you skip irrelevant characters?
Return the number of distinct shortest covering slices instead.
